record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: For each instance size n of the Stable Marriage problem, determine the maximum possible number x_n of stable matchings over all size-n instances, or at least substantially narrow the remaining gap between the best known lower and upper bounds on x_n.

evidence.quote: This open problem, first posed by Gusfield and Irving [45], concerns finding the maximum number xn of stable matchings admitted by any sm instance of size n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An instance of the Stable Marriage problem of size n consists of n men and n women, where each person has a strict total order (preference list) ranking all n members of the opposite sex. A matching M is a bijection between the set of men and the set of women. A pair (m,w) with M(m) ≠ w is called a blocking pair for M if m prefers w to M(m) and w prefers m to M(w). A matching M is stable if it admits no blocking pair.

For each positive integer n, let x_n denote the maximum, taken over all Stable Marriage instances of size n, of the number of distinct stable matchings admitted by the instance.

Determine x_n exactly for every n, or otherwise substantially narrow the gap between the best known lower and upper bounds on x_n. In particular, the current best lower bound is of the form Ω(c₁^n) with c₁ ≈ 2.28 (via the Irving–Leather construction) and the current best upper bound is simply exponential of the form c₂^n for some constant c₂; close the gap between these two constants, or determine the precise exponential growth rate of x_n.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open in its exact form. Karlin, Gharan, and Weber (STOC 2018, arXiv:1711.01032) established the first simply exponential upper bound c^n for the maximum number of stable matchings, improving on prior bounds of the form 2^(n log n - O(n)). The best lower bound, due to Irving and Leather, remains Ω(2.28^n). A gap between the bases of the exponents persists, and the exact growth rate of x_n is still unknown.

status_evidence.title: A Simply Exponential Upper Bound on the Maximum Number of Stable Matchings
status_evidence.snippet: We establish a simply exponential upper bound c^n on the maximum number of stable matchings in an instance of size n.
status_evidence.claim: The best known upper bound on x_n was improved to simply exponential c^n, but does not match the Ω(2.28^n) lower bound.

status_evidence.title: A Simply Exponential Upper Bound on the Maximum Number of Stable Matchings (STOC 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Improves the previous best upper bound of 2^{n log n - O(n)} to a simply exponential bound.
status_evidence.claim: Upper bound improved but exact value of x_n remains open.
